JMPR:
Maleic hydrazide (free)
The residue is not fat soluble
EU:
Reg. 396/2005: Maleic hydrazide
The residue is not fat soluble
efsa_comments:
Residue definition for enforcement is the same in the EU and derived by the JMPR.
The residue definition for risk assessment for plants in the EU is maleic hydrazide (restricted to foliar treatment on root crops only).
The latest peer‐review (EFSA, 2025i) considered the additional toxicological data available on 3‐pyridazinone leading to a separate ADI for this metabolite (see Section 1.1.2). Therefore, the expression of the risk assessment residue definition in animal commodities was proposed.
Due to an insufficient toxicological database, the JMPR could not perform a toxicological evaluation of maleic‐hydrazide or its metabolites. Therefore, the JMPR did not propose a RD‐RA for plants or livestock.

JMPR:
Sum of prochloraz, N‐propyl‐N‐[2‐(2,4,6‐ trichlorophenoxy)ethyl]urea (BTS 44595) and N‐formyl‐N‐propyl‐N‐[2‐(2,4,6‐trichlorophenoxy)ethyl]urea (BTS 44596), expressed as prochloraz
The residue is fat soluble
EU:
Reg. 396/2005: Prochloraz (sum of prochloraz, BTS 44595 (M201‐04) and BTS 44596 (M201‐03), expressed as prochloraz)
The residue is fat soluble
efsa_comments:
The residue definitions for MRL enforcement established by JMPR and in the EU are identical.
For the residue definition for risk assessment, the EU RDs for plant and animal products are a common moiety residue definition, while in the JMPR residue definitions two specific metabolites which were considered the main metabolites in plant and animal commodities were included; these metabolites are also covered by the EU common moiety RD. Additional three metabolites were considered for risk assessment (i.e. BTS44595, BTS44770, BTS54906); since the toxicological data were not sufficient for a full hazard characterisation, the exposure is compared to the threshold of toxicological concern, Cramer class III. These three metabolites are also covered by the EU common moiety RD.

JMPR:
Methoprene
The residue is fat soluble
EU:
Reg. 396/2005: Methoprene
No EU peer review and no MRL review
efsa_comments:
Residue definition for enforcement is the same in the EU and JMPR.
At EU level, no risk assessment residue definitions have been set since methoprene residue behaviour was never assessed in the EU.
Considering the log Pow, and the findings of animal metabolism/feeding studies, the modification of the residue definition, including the label (F) for fat‐soluble substances should be considered in the EU.
The residue definition of JMPR was based on metabolism studies in wheat (post‐harvest treatment), alfalfa and rice (both foliar application). No specific metabolism studies are available for fruits (post‐harvest treatment).

JMPR:
Sum of hexythiazox and all metabolites containing the trans‐5‐(4‐chlorophenyl)‐4‐methyl‐2‐oxothiazolidine‐moiety (PT‐1‐3), expressed as hexythiazox
The residue is fat soluble
EU:
Reg. 396/2005 Hexythiazox (any ratio of constituent isomers)
The residue is fat soluble
efsa_comments: The residue definition for enforcement in plants is similar at EU and JMPR levels. The residue definition for enforcement in animal products, as well as the risk assessment residue definitions in plant and animal commodities derived by JMPR, are wider as they include all metabolites containing the trans‐5‐(4‐ chlorophenyl)‐4‐methyl‐2‐oxothiazolidine‐moiety (PT‐1‐3).

The EU risk assessment residue definition for plant is wider, includes alpha‐CO. See also the consumer risk assessment.
The residue definition for risk assessment (animal products) is tentative, because the following data were not available in the MRL review:
–
metabolism studies in ruminants and poultry performed with the parent and the metabolite alpha‐CO;
–
a fully validated method for enforcement in kidney and liver;
–
storage stability studies investigating stability of etofenprox in eggs, milk and animal tissues others than liver.
Confirmatory data were requested under Regulation (EC) No 396/2005.
The RMS informed EFSA that the requested confirmatory data were submitted and were assessed in the renewal process. According to the RMS, a new metabolism study in laying hens and lactating goat with alpha‐CO (taking into account the metabolic behaviour of alpha‐CO and the lower toxicity compared to the parent compound) will be available for the renewal process.

JMPR:
Cyproconazole
The residue is fat soluble
EU:
PLAN/2023/1960 not yet applicable, Regulation implementing MRL review:
Cyproconazole (sum of isomers)
Reg. 396/2005: Cyproconazole
The residue is fat soluble
efsa_comments:
Residue definition for enforcement for plants and livestock is similar in the EU and JMPR.
The RD for RA for plants in the EU includes a separate RD for TDMs; the RD‐RA for livestock in the EU is more comprehensive as it includes metabolites M36(Z2), M38(Z1) and M9/M14.

Residue definitions for enforcement in plants and livestock in the EU and JMPR are comparable.
In the peer review, for the representative uses (tomatoes and pepper), the residue definition for risk assessment was set as flubendiamide, since residues of the metabolite flubendiamide‐des‐iodo was always below the LOQ in all tested samples (EFSA, 2013e). However, it was noted that the residue definition might be reconsidered, in case the use pattern is extended to crops where flubendiamide‐des‐iodo may occur at significant levels. In such case, as the toxicological data on this metabolite are limited (EFSA, 2013e), more information on its toxicological relevance would be required.
In the framework of the Art. 12 MRL review (EFSA, 2020i), considering the results of the metabolism studies, and that the metabolite flubendiamide‐des‐iodo was below the LOQ of 0.01 mg/kg in all the residue trials assessed, EFSA proposed that the residue definition for risk assessment as parent only was still appropriate for the uses assessed that included fruits and fruiting vegetables, roots and tubers, leafy vegetables, pulses and oilseeds, cereals and rice (EFSA, 2020i).

JMPR: Sum of fosetyl, phosphonic acid and their salts, expressed as phosphonic acid
EU: MRL review (EFSA, 2021l) and Peer review (EFSA, 2018c): Sum of fosetyl, phosphonic acid and their salts, expressed as phosphonic acid
efsa_comments:
The existing enforcement residue definitions set by JMPR includes also fosetyl, while in the EU for plant and animal commodities includes only phosphonic acid and their salts, expressed as phosphonic acid. However, fosetyl is rapidly degrading to phosphonic acid in plants and in animals. Thus, the difference of the enforcement residue definition for plant products is of low practical relevance.
The residue definitions for risk assessment in commodities of plant and animal origin proposed by the EU peer review (EFSA, 2018c) and that were used in the Art. 12/Art. 43 MRL joint review for fosetyl, disodium phosphonate and potassium phosphonate (EFSA, 2021l) are the same as the ones derived by the JMPR.
In the updated peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of fosetyl (EFSA, 2025d), aluminium is proposed to be included separately in the plant residue definition for risk assessment.
